blocks.text: Network calls fail for many reasons that have nothing to do with your code. A server may be restarting, a load balancer may drop a connection, or the client may hit a rate limit. Instead of showing every failure to the user, the client can opt in to automatic retries with `retry: true`.

Retries are only safe when a request is idempotent, which means that sending it twice has the same effect as sending it once. A `GET` request is idempotent by definition, but a `POST` that charges a credit card is not. Under the hood, the client attaches an idempotency key so that the server can discard duplicates.
Wait a little longer after each attempt (exponential backoff).
Add random jitter so that thousands of clients do not retry at the same moment.
One caveat: a retry cannot fix a request that is wrong, so 4xx errors are returned right away.
